title.value: Why do sleep disorders belong to mental disorder classifications? A network analysis of the “Sleep-Wake Disorders” section of the DSM-5
title.justification: The title of the paper is directly extracted from the source provided.
title.quote: Why do sleep disorders belong to mental disorder classifications? A network analysis of the “Sleep-Wake Disorders” section of the DSM-5

analysis.description: This paper investigates how sleep disorders are classified within the DSM-5 by using network analysis on the diagnostic criteria of the "Sleep-Wake Disorders" section of the DSM-5. The study extracts symptoms, builds a network representation, and quantifies its structure to analyze the position of sleep disorders in mental disorders.

type.justification: The study conducts an empirical investigation by extracting symptoms and building a network representation of the "Sleep-Wake Disorders" section in DSM-5.
type.quote: We hypothesize that the analysis of the most central symptoms will allow us to better analyze the position of Sleep disorders in Mental disorders. We thus i) extracted the symptoms of the DSM-5 diagnostic criteria of Sleep-Wake disorders, ii) built the Sleep-Wake disorder DSM-5 network representation, and iii) quantified its structure at local and global levels using classical symptom network analysis.

name.justification: The paper applies network analysis methods to psychiatric classifications, specifically within the context of sleep disorders.
name.quote: This article proposes to investigate how Sleep disorders have been conceptualized within the DSM-5 through symptom network analysis of the diagnostic criteria of the “Sleep-Wake Disorders” section in the DSM-5.

name.justification: The paper focuses on analyzing the classification of sleep disorders within the DSM-5.
name.quote: Thirty-four different symptoms were identified among the 53 DSM-5 diagnostic criteria of the 9 main disorders of the “Sleep-Wake Disorders” section.

name.justification: The study is in the context of understanding sleep disorders as a part of mental disorder classifications.
name.quote: This network analysis shown that the belonging of Sleep-Wake disorders in the DSM-5 have been associated with central sleep symptoms considered as “Mental”, given their phenomenality (qualitative nature of the experience) and subjectivity (in personal mental lives).
